title: FCNR Deposits Offer NRIs Up to 7% Returns, but Home-Country Taxes May Shrink the Yield
excerpt: India's RBI-backed swap window has pushed FCNR deposit rates to multi-year highs, yet NRIs in the US, UK and Singapore face sharply different after-tax outcomes depending on where they file returns.
body:
• RBI's special swap facility has lifted FCNR deposit rates to 5.7–7.1% for 3-to-5-year terms, well above equivalent US CD rates of 2–4%.
  • FCNR interest is tax-free in India under Section 10(15)(iv)(fa), but NRIs must still report and pay tax in their country of residence — US-based NRIs face federal rates of 10–37%, while the UK now taxes worldwide income for all residents after four years.
  • Singapore's territorial tax system generally exempts overseas interest for individuals, making it the most favourable jurisdiction among the three for FCNR depositors.

RBI Window Pushes FCNR Rates to Multi-Year Highs

The Reserve Bank of India's June 2026 swap facility has transformed the economics of Foreign Currency Non-Resident deposits. By absorbing the hedging cost that banks normally bear when converting foreign-currency inflows into rupee lending, the RBI has freed banks to raise rates sharply. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Bank of Baroda now offer peak rates of 6% on three-to-five-year dollar deposits — a jump of up to 310 basis points, according to Livemint. Smaller banks quote rates in the 7–7.1% range.

https://x.com/Normal_2610/status/2080329624052171161

The window applies to deposits mobilised between 8 June and 30 September 2026, with a one-year lock-in. Banks are expected to raise $30–50 billion in fresh FCNR deposits by the deadline, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

The Indian Tax Shield — and Its Limits

Interest earned on FCNR deposits is exempt from Indian income tax under Section 10(15)(iv)(fa) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, as long as the depositor holds NRI or RNOR status. No TDS applies. But the exemption addresses only half the equation.

"The interest is tax-free in India, but a US-resident NRI still reports it to the IRS, while an NRI in the UAE keeps the full rate. The same deposit is a strong proposition in the Gulf and a more modest one in America."

— Animesh Hardia, Senior Vice President, 1 Finance

US: Federal Tax Bites Into Returns

For US-resident NRIs, foreign interest income is added to total worldwide income and taxed at federal slab rates of 10–37%. The India-US DTAA does not exempt this interest from US tax; since India already exempts it, the full US liability applies.

An NRI in the 22–24% federal bracket booking a 7% FCNR deposit would see an after-tax yield of roughly 5.3–5.5%, according to 1 Finance. State income taxes in California or New York would shave that further. The spread over a comparable three-year US CD narrows but does not vanish.

"For a US resident NRI or OCI who wants to park money for three years as part of their long-term debt allocation in USD terms, FCNR deposits are definitely a good option right now."

— Deepak Shenoy, CEO, Capital Mind MF

UK: Worldwide Taxation After Four Years

The UK's tax landscape shifted from 6 April 2025, when HMRC replaced the domicile-based remittance regime with the Foreign Income and Gains (FIG) system. Individuals UK-resident for more than four tax years are now taxed on worldwide income as it arises — regardless of domicile. FCNR interest falls squarely within this net.

UK income tax rates on savings income above the personal savings allowance run from 20% to 45%. An NRI in the higher-rate bracket at 40% earning 7% on an FCNR deposit would retain just 4.2% after tax. The India-UK DTAA allows credit for tax paid in the source country, but since India charges nothing on FCNR interest, there is no credit to claim.

Singapore: The Favourable Outlier

Singapore follows a territorial approach to individual income tax. For most residents, overseas income received in Singapore is generally not taxable. FCNR interest, classified as foreign-sourced income, typically falls outside the tax net for individuals.

HDFC Bank's Singapore-focused FCNR guide notes exceptions where income flows through a local partnership or is connected with a Singapore business. But for the typical salaried NRI, India's exemption and Singapore's territorial exclusion mean FCNR interest can effectively be received tax-free in both jurisdictions. HDFC Bank quotes SGD FCNR rates of 3.40% for three-to-five-year deposits — lower than USD rates because the swap facility is dollar-specific.

What NRIs Should Weigh

Financial advisors urge NRIs to compare after-tax returns in their country of residence, not headline Indian rates. The deposit's one-year lock-in, premature withdrawal penalties — Federal Bank charges 1% on the applicable rate — and the absence of foreign deposit insurance add layers of consideration.

For NRIs with a three-to-five-year horizon who can commit surplus foreign-currency savings, current FCNR rates represent a clear opportunity. But its size depends less on what India charges — which is nothing — and more on what the IRS, HMRC or IRAS expects at the other end.
